# DSH TaskBridge — Codex Native Skill

Read this entry in full. Open [the reference](rules-reference-4f0bd526845ddddd198259a31dfbbed55d4aaaf88b793e210808330bcb7d7e7a.md) only for multi-stage or
parallel planning, a dirty source, an explicit teams choice, task reuse, or a non-`ready` event.

## ACTIVATION (check this before anything else)
1. Dispatch only when the user explicitly selects this skill (`$dsh-taskbridge`) or explicitly
   asks to delegate a Git repository code implementation or verification task to DSH / TaskBridge.
2. Casual mention of DSH, DeepSeek, dsh-taskbridge or delegation — or a general non-code Q&A
   (e.g. checking the time or ordinary chat, even if `$dsh-taskbridge` or `@dsh-taskbridge` is
   mentioned), or a question about planning, review, status, logs or settings — is NOT a dispatch
   request. Answer directly in Codex (noting that TaskBridge is only for Git repository
   code/verification tasks) without calling any `delegate_*` tool.
3. If assignment is ambiguous, ask one short clarifying question instead of dispatching.

## CODE MODE CALLS
Keep skill reads separate from large outputs. Avoid dumping `ALL_TOOLS`. For a missing field, find
one tool by exact name and print only the text from `exec tool declaration:` if present.
Omit unused optional keys. Use `const data = JSON.parse(res.content[0].text)` and handle
`res.isError` or `data.ok !== true` before acting. Keep the receipts and follow the returned `reason`.

Check status first; run read-only preflight separately:

```js
text(await tools.mcp__dsh_delegate__delegate_status({}));
```

```js
text(await tools.mcp__dsh_delegate__delegate_preflight({ workspacePath }));
```

## P0: COMMANDER-OWNED PLANNING AND WORK PACKETS (DECOMPOSITION & DIRECTION)
1. Codex owns decomposition, direction, scope boundaries and acceptance — NOT line-by-line coding
   details. Batch read-only inspection of key entry files, specs and existing contracts into 1–2
   combined reads before dispatching. Submit a cohesive task that DSH can complete and verify in
   one shot as a single packet without `delegate_plan`; split large or multi-stage goals into
   bounded, independently verifiable packets only when a single packet risks overloading the
   worker across subsystems or when independent modules can run in parallel.
2. Before dispatch, tell the operator which packet is next and why. Invest upfront in a thorough
   contract brief in `delegate_submit.prompt` so the worker passes on the first try without rework:
   (a) target outcome and repo spec/doc paths to follow; (b) architectural direction, exact
   exported signatures, closed return-object keys (no unrequested fields or input mutation), and
   concrete spec/runtime invariants where workers commonly slip — exact decimal string/rational
   scaling (never `BigInt(float * scale)` or intermediate float rounding), own-property map
   lookups (`Object.hasOwn`), exact default semantics per spec (`??` vs `=== undefined` rather than
   `||` swallowing valid `''`/`0`/`false`), full domain/enum
   validation (e.g. supported currency/status sets, UTC full-year dates), and error-reporting vs
   throwing on malformed records (concise 3–5 line mathematical/serialization invariants are
   encouraged whenever ambiguity could cause drift); (c) allowed edit scope and out-of-scope red
   lines; (d) concrete acceptance tests/checks, requiring real child-process CLI entrypoint/exit-code
   tests and `os.tmpdir()` scratch directories (never checkout-local temp dirs or mocked `main()`
   even if the worker sandbox restricts subprocesses). **Do NOT dictate line-by-line implementation
   code, internal variable names, or full pseudocode in `prompt`** — let DSH read the repo and own
   implementation and test coding within those guardrails.
3. Parallel packets require independent work, non-conflicting ownership and permission under the
   request and repository AGENTS.md. Never expand scope or let a verification-only packet modify
   code or rules.

## DISPATCH CONTRACT
1. **PREFLIGHT (new task chains only)**. Call `delegate_status` first (once per session); if the
   switch is off or a prerequisite is missing, report the reason and pause. Never open the switch
   yourself or fall back to another execution route.
   - For read-only workspace validation or checking multiple/uncertain directories, call
     `delegate_preflight` directly with the exact authorized source `workspacePath`. For a normal
     single-repo dispatch, you may pass `autoPreflight: true, wait: true` on `delegate_submit` to
     combine preflight, submit and wait in one call (blocks cleanly without submitting on any block
     reason; if it returns `submitted: true` with `waitError`, the task WAS already created — never
     call `delegate_submit` again, and resume with `delegate_wait` on `submitReceipt.taskId`). Reuse
     verified preflight facts for a same-chain `continueFromTaskId` continuation (or
     `reuseWorktreeFromTaskId` subtask) and never repeat `delegate_status` / `delegate_preflight`
     on the same source repo unless the source changed or the engine reports a mismatch.
   - `isolation: "worktree"`: omit `overrides` so the configured isolation and matching project
     override apply.
   - Both `worktree` and `shared` isolation require an initialized Git repository root with at
     least one commit. Any other `isolation: "block"` (`PREFLIGHT_NOT_A_REPOSITORY`,
     `PREFLIGHT_NOT_A_REPOSITORY_ROOT`, `PREFLIGHT_NO_COMMITS`): stop and report the reason code
     (and any reported repository root), and never take over coding locally.
2. **SUBMIT**. Set a short `title` (plus optional `goalDescription`), exact authorized
   `workspacePath`, and the P0 direction brief in `prompt`. Never override the configured provider,
   model or reasoning effort, and never send `overrides.timeoutSeconds` unless the operator
   explicitly asked for a cap (normal runs have no default total execution timeout).
3. **RECEIPT CHECK**. From `delegate_submit` (or `submitReceipt` when `wait: true`) and the first
   actionable wait/result receipt, verify source path, `executionWorkspacePath`, isolation, DSH
   workspace/session identity, and `agentTeams` / `agentTeamsOrigin` / `team.applied` /
   `team.enabled`. Pause dependent dispatches and report any mismatch.

For a normal single repo, submit and wait in one script:

```js
// @exec: {"yield_time_ms": 1200000}
text(await tools.mcp__dsh_delegate__delegate_submit({ workspacePath, title, prompt, autoPreflight: true, wait: true }));
```

## WAIT & EVENTS (SINGLE DIRECT CHAIN IN THIS SESSION)
**Direct single-chain wait — NO `spawn_agent` / `wait_agent` wrapper**. Omit `waitSeconds` (default 3600 seconds,
Codex tool timeout 3660 seconds). A shorter wait is only for an explicitly requested one-off diagnostic.
Never poll `delegate_status` or `delegate_result` during a wait. The cadence
belongs to the tool, not to you. Resume an existing task with its `taskId`.

```js
// @exec: {"yield_time_ms": 1200000}
text(await tools.mcp__dsh_delegate__delegate_wait({ taskId }));
```

- Prefer a direct blocking MCP call when Codex exposes one. In Code Mode, set a long outer yield
  before the first call that waits, and keep it for every continuation, including waits after a
  permission decision or a question answer. Where supported and allowed by the host, start the
  `functions.exec` script with `// @exec: {"yield_time_ms": 1200000}`. Prefer a supported yield
  that covers the full MCP wait when the host offers one.
- If Code Mode returns `Script running with cell ID`, keep the existing MCP call active. If the
  host offers automatic continuation, let the tool layer resume it. Otherwise call
  `functions.wait` on the same `cell_id` with the same long `yield_time_ms`. Keep waiting for the
  MCP answer or agreed deadline. If the host requires short yields and model-driven continuation,
  tell the operator once that waiting will wake the model at each yield.

- `wait-limit` — THIS call's own wait budget ran out (`actionable: false` and `terminal: false`):
  call `delegate_wait` on the same `taskId` immediately.
- `heartbeat`: nothing to report — call `delegate_wait` on the same `taskId`.
- `ready`: execution finished — this is not acceptance. Call `delegate_result` ONCE (pass
  `includeDiff: false` when reviewing locally in `executionWorkspacePath` to avoid duplicating
  patches in context; paginate omitted notes/summaries only if needed). Review in Codex, then
  call `delegate_review` (`accepted` or `changes-requested`, `note`, optional
  `completionSummary`, `receiptOnly: true`) and confirm `reviewPersistence.state === "saved"`
  (`reviewPersistence.durable === true`; if `saving`/`timed-out`, report honestly; if `failed`,
  retry). Consolidate defects into ONE follow-up via `continueFromTaskId`.

Read the complete matching reference section for a client timeout, `attention`, `permission` (note:
Codex's own `approval_policy` never forbids granting `allow-once` to a safe in-scope worker test/Git
command with `allowBlocked: null`), `question`, `failed`, `cancelled`, or `interrupted`. Use its
control section for an explicit inspection or stop request during a blocking wait.

## DO NOT IMPLEMENT LOCALLY WHILE A DELEGATED WORKER RUNS
Never commit, stash, branch, reset or edit locally while a delegated task is running, waiting or
awaiting review (single-writer guarantee). The ONLY exception is an explicit user-authorized
takeover — never a long silence, a permission refusal, a failed run or your own judgement. While
you are waiting, stay silent and do NOT narrate snapshots that have not changed (except for work
INDEPENDENT of the delegated task, an inspection the operator explicitly asked for, or a blocked
diagnosis).

## REVIEW BOUNDARY (PRAGMATIC ACCEPTANCE)
1. Report task state, actual provider/model/effort from the result, confirmed `agentTeams` /
   `agentTeamsOrigin` / `team.applied` / `team.enabled`, actual execution directory, DSH
   workspace/session identity, changed-file summary, verification evidence and limitations. Codex
   remains responsible for reviewing changes/tests, accepting or requesting changes, and deciding
   any follow-up. Never commit, push, or read/store/relay credentials or connection tokens.
2. **Pragmatic acceptance bar (prevent nitpick rework)**: judge against the designated test suite,
   explicit spec contracts, error codes and documented boundaries. Request changes
   (`changes-requested`, consolidated into ONE follow-up via `continueFromTaskId`, freezing
   dependent downstream packets) ONLY for genuine spec/requirement violations, real functional or
   edge-case bugs, failing/missing required tests, out-of-scope edits, or leftover temp/junk files.
   **Do NOT invent adversarial out-of-spec fuzz probes** (e.g. 16-digit IEEE-754 ULP boundaries,
   inputs beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, or null-prototype objects when not in spec) to reject
   passing deliveries. Consolidate all defects in the first review (converging within 1 rework
   round); record minor style preferences or out-of-spec extremes as non-blocking notes and accept
   (`accepted`).

## LOCAL VERIFICATION
After `ready`, call `tools.mcp__dsh_delegate__delegate_result({ taskId, includeDiff: false })` once.
In the same exec, check `!res.isError`, `data.ok === true`, then match the task and checkout receipt
to the authorized source and saved submission/wait receipts. Stop on missing or conflicting evidence.
Only then run one combined check in the verified `executionWorkspacePath`. Capture
`git rev-parse --short HEAD`, `git status --short`, `git diff --stat`, `git diff --check` and the
designated tests. Read relevant changed code with bounded output.

After verifying, send the review and check durable persistence. On the final `accepted` `worktree`
task (omit on `changes-requested` or intermediate subtasks), pass `applyToSource: true` so
TaskBridge syncs changes to `sourcePath` without committing; never copy, patch, or re-test there
yourself. Once `sourceSync.applied === true`, do not run extra hash or git checks in `sourcePath`.
Report `sourceSync` (`applied`, `reason`, `conflictingPaths`) and `executionWorkspacePath`.

```js
text(await tools.mcp__dsh_delegate__delegate_review({ taskId, decision, note, receiptOnly: true, applyToSource: true }));
```
